dim_sets.name: kw_ids
dim_sets.structure: flat_array<int32>(4) used as membership via std::unordered_set<int32> for mk.keyword_id test

dim_sets.name: cn_notus_bitset
dim_sets.notes: Scan company_name once: for each row read country_code slice, set bit at id if (slice != '[us]' AND slice non-empty). NULL/empty country_code: keep convention used by JOB Q22 family — treat NULL as != '[us]' (set bit). Probe in mc by bitset[mc.company_id].

join_order.notes: First fact probe: cheapest filter; if no mk row in [lo,hi) has keyword_id in kw_ids -> skip title.

join_order.build: it1_id (single id) + mi.info string set (10 strings)
join_order.strategy: csr_range_scan; for each row test info_type_id == it1_id, then test info string membership via std::unordered_set<std::string_view>
join_order.notes: Order: cheap int compare first, varlen string compare only on match.

join_order.strategy: csr_range_scan; for each row test info_type_id == it2_id; if match, compare info < '8.5' lex; project info for MIN(mi_idx.info)
join_order.notes: Need at least one matching row; for MIN(mi_idx.info), all surviving rows feed running min.

join_order.build: cn_notus_bitset + ct table (4 rows, no filter -> any company_type_id passes)
join_order.strategy: csr_range_scan; for each row: company_id valid index into cn bitset && cn_notus_bitset[company_id]; then read cn.name via company_name__id__pos[company_id] for MIN(cn.name)
join_order.notes: No filter on ct (any of 4 company_types accepted); skip ct lookup entirely.

data_structures.kw_ids: std::unordered_set<int32_t> (4 entries) — also acceptable: sorted small array with linear scan
data_structures.fact_csr_offsets: mmap uint64_t[2528314] for each of mk/mi/mi_idx/mc
data_structures.aggregation: three thread-local mins: int sentinels for strings use empty/UINT64_MAX, then merge at end

parallelism.reduction: per-thread (min_cn_name, min_mi_idx_info, min_t_title) merged with lexicographic min at end

indexes.purpose: id->row for reading cn.name on surviving mc rows
(optional) only used during literal resolution; not needed at probe time since we test t.kind_id ∈ {kt_ids}

projection.MIN(cn.name): varlen lex min — only read cn.name when a surviving (t,mk,mi,mi_idx,mc) tuple is confirmed
projection.MIN(mi_idx.info): varlen lex min — read mi_idx.info value already in hand during mi_idx probe (defer materialization until full tuple confirmed)
projection.MIN(t.title): varlen lex min — read t.title only when a surviving tuple is confirmed

execution_notes: Per title t: (1) check production_year>2005 and kind_id∈kt_ids; (2) probe mk CSR, require any mk.keyword_id ∈ kw_ids; (3) probe mi CSR, require any (mi.info_type_id==it1_id AND mi.info ∈ country_set); (4) probe mi_idx CSR, collect all matching mi_idx.info values (info_type_id==it2_id AND info<'8.5'); (5) probe mc CSR, collect all matching mc.company_id with cn_notus_bitset[company_id]==1; (6) if all four non-empty, update three running mins: min(t.title), min over collected mi_idx.info values, min over cn.name lookups.
Order of probes chosen by selectivity: mk (smallest CSR ranges + tiny kw set) -> mi -> mi_idx -> mc. Bail at first empty probe.
Do NOT materialize cn.name or t.title unless all four facts produced at least one matching tuple.
